Q1.title: Quiz 1 · Production and sectors of production

items.p: What is production?
items.a: The process of making goods and providing services
w: The process of selling goods at a lower price
The process of saving money in a bank
The process of buying raw materials only
items.ref: Production is the process of making goods and providing services.

items.p: Which of these is an example of non-durable goods?
items.a: Food
items.ref: Non-durable goods are consumed once or used in a short period of time, like food.

items.p: Which factor of production means human skills and work effort?
items.a: Labour
items.ref: Labour: human skills and work effort.

items.p: Which sector converts raw materials into semi-finished or finished goods?
items.a: The secondary sector
items.ref: The secondary sector converts raw materials into semi-finished or finished goods (manufacturing, building, clothing, food).

items.p: What is responsible sourcing?
items.a: Considering social and environmental responsibilities when managing suppliers
w: Buying raw materials always at the lowest price
items.ref: Responsible sourcing means that companies consider their social and environmental responsibilities when managing relationships with suppliers.

items.p: What happens to the unit cost when a business expands its scale of production?
items.a: It decreases
items.ref: When a business expands its scale of production, there is a decrease in the unit cost.

items.p: Why do fixed costs help to create economies of scale?
items.a: They are distributed across a higher number of units
w: They grow with every unit produced
They are paid only by small businesses
They are paid by the government
items.ref: Fixed costs, like rent and administration, are distributed across a higher number of units.

items.p: Buying in bulk is an example of…
items.a: an internal economy of scale
items.ref: Internal economies of scale come from the business itself: buying in bulk means a lower price per item.

items.p: Similar companies in the same geographical area, like the Ceramic Valley, are an example of…
items.a: clustering
items.ref: Clustering is an external economy of scale: similar companies in the same geographical area.

items.p: Which of these is a way to solve diseconomies of scale?
items.a: Outsourcing certain processes to third-party providers
w: Hiring more managers without a plan
items.ref: Diseconomies of scale can be solved with more efficient production, leaner administration and outsourcing.

Q3.title: Quiz 3 · Quality control and smart manufacturing

items.p: What does quality control (QC) ensure?
items.a: That products meet standards of quality and safety before they are sold
w: That products are always the cheapest on the market
That products are sold only abroad
That workers do not need training
items.ref: QC ensures that products meet certain standards of quality and safety before they are sold to the public.

items.p: Which of these is typically part of quality control?
items.a: Visual inspections and testing of materials
items.ref: QC typically consists of visual inspections, testing of materials and equipment to detect defects.

items.p: Smart manufacturing is typical of…
items.a: Industry 4.0
items.ref: Smart manufacturing is typical of Industry 4.0, where machines and production systems are interconnected.

items.p: What do collaborative robots show?
items.a: Human-machine interaction
items.ref: Human-machine interaction: people and automated systems work together to achieve shared goals (e.g. collaborative robots).

items.p: What is a digital twin?
items.a: A virtual replica used for testing
w: A second factory in another country
A worker who does two jobs
items.ref: Augmented reality can create digital twins, virtual replicas for testing purposes.

items.p: Why do large companies move some production activities to other countries?
items.a: For lower labour costs and easier access to resources
w: To be further from their target markets
items.ref: Companies relocate for easier access to resources, lower labour costs, environmental regulations and market access.

items.p: What is offshoring?
items.a: Relocating business processes to different international locations due to lower costs
w: Returning production to the country of origin
items.ref: Offshoring: relocating business processes or operations to different international locations due to lower costs.

items.p: Moving customer service to another country is an example of…
items.a: service offshoring
items.ref: Service offshoring is the relocation of support processes, like IT and customer service.

items.p: How is outsourcing different from offshoring?
items.a: Outsourcing uses external organisations, but not necessarily in another country
w: Outsourcing always happens in another country
items.ref: Outsourcing involves contracting work out to external organisations, but it doesn't have to be in another country.

items.p: What is reshoring?
items.a: When a business returns production to the country of origin
w: When a business moves production abroad
When a business buys in bulk
items.ref: Reshoring: when a business returns production or operations to the country of origin. It is the reverse of offshoring.

items.p: What does the circular economy consist in?
items.a: Reusing and recycling materials to reduce consumption and waste
w: Throwing products away after one use
items.ref: The circular economy consists in reusing and recycling materials to reduce consumption of raw materials and minimise waste and pollution.

items.p: In the linear economy, raw materials are…
items.a: extracted, used and then thrown away
items.ref: In the linear economy raw materials are extracted, used and then thrown away.

items.p: The circular economy is an answer to which problems?
items.a: Climate change, waste and pollution
items.ref: Circular economy is an answer to the problems of climate change, waste and pollution.

items.p: In the technical cycle, products last longer thanks to…
items.a: reusing, repairing and recycling
items.ref: Technical cycle: products and materials last longer thanks to reusing, repairing and recycling.

items.p: What happens in the biological cycle?
items.a: Nutrients from biodegradable materials are returned to the Earth
items.ref: Biological cycle: the nutrients from biodegradable materials are returned to the Earth.
